summary: Gyatsho Tshering (1936–2009) was a scholar in Tibetology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its Acting Director in 1972 and Director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda (1867–1954) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926–1944), commissioned professor at the University of Tokyo in 1928, and lecturer at Toyo University.

Gyoei Takahashi (b. 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as assistant professor (attested 2003–2004) and professor (attested 2026) at Rissho University, and was a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

Gyoko Iotani (b. 1949) studied at Rissho University (~1968–1978), where he worked as assistant professor (~1980–1990), professor (~1990–2015), and professor emeritus (~2015). He was also a former specially appointed professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyokusen Hosaka (1887–1964) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1908–1913). He served as president of Komazawa Junior College from around 1950 to 1964.
Gyomay Kubose (1905–2000) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu from around 1936 to 1941.
Gyoon Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015). He held the post of deputy director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyosho Takahashi (b. 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).
Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhism at Minobusan University (attested 2001).

Gyula Benigny (1890–1966) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University (~1908–1912). He taught at Debrecen Reformed Theological University (~1914) and served at the University of Debrecen as Docent (1917) and extraordinary Professor (1932–1949).
Gyula Ortutay (1910–1978) studied at the University of Szeged between 1928 and 1934 and held a post at Nyugat.
Gyula Wojtilla (b. 1945) is an Indologist who studied under János Harmatta (~1963–1968) and at Eötvös Loránd University (1964–1969). He also studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1973–1974).

Gyurme Dorje (1950–2020) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at George Watson's College, Edinburgh (MA), and SOAS (Ph.D. under Philip Denwood), he held fellowships at SOAS and the University of London, and translated for the Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Pema Tekchok studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

György Hazai (1932–2016) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1949–1954) and held a post at the Institut für Orientforschung (~1970–1983).

György Kara (1935–2022) studied at Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University. He held positions at Eötvös Loránd University, directed at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1975–2000), and was a professor at Indiana University (1993–2022).

Gyōin Hashimoto (1897–1978) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1921–1925) and under Join Saeki. He served as head priest of Yakushiji (1939–1967) and superintendent of the Hosso School (1940).

Gábor Kovács is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Dharma Gate Buddhist College (MA 2005–2010) and Corvinus University of Budapest (PhD 2010–2017). He became an associate professor at Corvinus University of Budapest in 2018.
Gé Mang Khenchen Yönten Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Shechen Gyaltsab.

Gérard Barrigue de Fontainieu (1863–1927) was an Indology scholar who completed his diploma at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales by 1891. He served as a pensionnaire at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1901–1902).
